newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah little changed in sleepy trade.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah little changed in sleepy trade.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was little changed against the dollar in late Monday trade, dealers said.
"There is barely any trade. People are mainly staying on the sidelines because of the absence of Singapore players and also due to a public holiday in the United States," one said.
The Japanese bank dealer said sentiment on the rupiah was still firm despite ample money market liquidity.
Overnight money was traded at 9.0/10.0 percent.
Spot rupiah was at 2,334.0/34.5 at 0845 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,334.00/34.75. Tomorrow was at 2,333.50/33.75.
"The prices quoted today were not attractive. It's a bit too wide, suggesting people are in no mood to trade," he said.
Dealers said there was some extended dollar selling in the morning from Friday following the central bank governor's statement that he would not use foreign exchange to boost export competitiveness.
But the downside of the dollar was limited due to ample rupiah supply which triggered some buying, they said.
The liquidity outlook was mixed, with one- and two-week money seen edging up while one-month money trending down.
Dealers said swap trading remained quiet in the afternoon.
